questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: You can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Provide you with an escape route.
Welcome other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Welcome other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to stay safe. Position yourself to avoid blind spots, help others see you, avoid road hazards, avoid wind from other vehicles, and have an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will NOT try to share your lane.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: As a new rider, when following another vehicle you should:

options.text: Keep at least a four-second distance between you and the vehicle.
Get as close to the other vehicle as possible.
Never worry about your following distance.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least a four-second distance between you and the vehicle.
questions.explanation: New riders should maintain at least a four-second following distance. Increase this distance whenever conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Signs about road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When entering a turn, it is best to:

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, they should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.

questions.explanation: When a group of motorcyclists passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Protects more than just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects more than just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, downshift and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind. If a larger animal is in your path, slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed at or below the posted speed limit. You can only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Encourage friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can prevent drunk driving by arranging other transportation, involving friends to help stop them, and slowing their drinking. Telling them to use less-crowded roads is not a safe solution.

questions.question: Which of these provides the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not adequate protection.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle, where should the heavier items go?

options.text: Lighter items should be stored in front of you.

questions.explanation: Pack heavier items toward the front of the load. Position loads over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you reduce your crash risk?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.

questions.explanation: Make yourself as visible as possible by wearing bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: If you are carrying a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with you during turns. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When being passed, which is NOT a potential hazard?

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors hitting you. Also be aware of wind gusts and objects that passengers might throw. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: When should a passenger mount a motorcycle?

options.text: As far back on the motorcycle as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should board only after the engine is running and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rear brake on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to driving a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle uses the same basic techniques as a car. However, motorcycles are harder to see. Because motorcycles are small, they can easily hide in another vehicle's blind spot. Other drivers may not notice you even when looking.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: The best way to help others see you at an intersection is to keep your headlight on. Your headlight should always be on when your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Stop other drivers from passing you.
Stay in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Your lane position protects your space and shows other drivers your intentions.

questions.question: A major effect of drinking alcohol is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both physical and mental body functions.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's safety distance should:

options.text: Change based on road and traffic conditions.
Not be necessary in most situations.
Be avoided to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more distance behind other vehicles if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy.
